'''Elisabeth Bouchaud''' (born Tibi) is a French [[physicist]], [[playwright]] and [[actress]] born 1 March 1961. She is a former member of [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique]] (CEA), and of [[Ecole Superieure de Chimie et Physique de la Ville de Paris]]. Since 2014, she is also the Director of the Théâtre de la Reine Blanche in Paris.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.reineblanche.com|title=La Reine Blanche |date= |access-date=2015-03-01}}</ref> In 2019, she opened a theatre in Avignon.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.reineblanche.com/pages/avignon |title=Avignon-Reine Blanche}}</ref> That same year, she also created a drama school,<ref>{{cite web|url= https://lasalleblanchetheatre.com/ |title=La Salle Blanche}}</ref> with [[:fr:Florient Azoulay]] and [[:fr:Xavier Gallais]]

In physics, she has worked in quantitative [[fractography]], establishing some ''universal'' [[fractal]] properties of fracture surfaces,<ref>[http://newsoffice.mit.edu/2011/scratch-test-0602 "Researchers redefine the old ‘scratch test’"]. Denise Brehm, ''MIT News'', June 2, 2011</ref> a subject pioneered by [[Benoit Mandelbrot]].<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Mandelbrot B, Passoja D, Paullay A |title=Fractal character of fracture surfaces of metals |journal=Nature |volume=308 |pages=721–22 |year=1984 |doi=10.1038/308721a0 |issue=5961|bibcode = 1984Natur.308..721M |s2cid=4330238 }}</ref> In fact, the term "fractal" itself was coined by Mandelbrot in 1975, based on the Latin frāctus meaning "broken" or "fractured".

[[Image:FractalLandscape.jpg|right|thumb|A close-up on a crack surface looks very much like this fractal landscape.]]

Elisabeth Bouchaud suggested that these fractal properties could be understood in terms of the [[Crack propagation|propagation]] of the crack front in a disordered environment, which is affected by the vicinity of a [[depinning transition]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Bouchaud E|title=Scaling properties of cracks |journal=Journal of Physics C |volume=9 |pages=4319–44 |year=1997 |url=http://www.ingentaconnect.com/content/iop/jphyscm/1997/00000009/00000021/art00002}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Bonamy D, Bouchaud E |title=Failure of heterogeneous materials: A dynamic phase transition? |journal=Physics Reports |volume=498 |issue=1 |pages=1–44 |year=2011 |bibcode=2011PhR...498....1B |doi=10.1016/j.physrep.2010.07.006}}</ref>

She was awarded the [[Louis Ancel Prize]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sfp.in2p3.fr/Prix/prix.html#ancel |title=Prix de la SFP |publisher=Sfp.in2p3.fr |date= |access-date=2013-10-16}}</ref> the [[Onsager Medal]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ntnu.no/fysikk/onsager2010 |title=Onsager professor 2010 - Aktuelt - Institutt for fysikk - NTNU |publisher=Ntnu.no |access-date=2013-10-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111010040745/http://www.ntnu.no/fysikk/onsager2010 |archive-date=2011-10-10 }}</ref> and the Aniuta Winter-Klein Prize.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-dsm.cea.fr/Phocea/Vie_des_labos/Ast/ast.php?t=actualites&id_ast=206 |title=Prix Aniuta Winter-Klein 2013, décerné à Elisabeth Bouchaud |publisher=Dsm.cea.fr |date= |access-date=2013-10-16}}</ref>

In 2025, for her work at La Reine Blanche, she was awarded the Jean Perrin Prize of Honour.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.sfphysique.fr/elisabeth-bouchaud-laureate-du-prix-jean-perrin-d-honneur-de-la-sfp/|title=Elisabeth Bouchaud Lauréate du Prix Jean Perrin}}</ref> She was also named one of the 100 Women of Culture of the Year 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.femmesdeculture.com/accueil|title= Femmes de Culture 2025}}</ref>

== Literary works ==

Elisabeth Bouchaud wrote several short stories and plays. 
Her first two plays - « Dangerous liaisons », after [[Choderlos de Laclos]], and « The tragedy of Medea -- bad blood » <ref>{{cite book|author=A. J. Boyle|title=Seneca: Medea: Edited with Introduction, Translation, and Commentary|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=W7icAgAAQBAJ&pg=PR140|date=January 2014|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-960208-7|pages=140–}}</ref> were written in 1991 and 1992 respectively. « The tragedy of Medea - bad blood » was performed at The Playroom <ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.adctheatre.com/about-us/corpus-playroom/|title=The Playroom}}</ref> in Cambridge, under the direction of Richard Bridge. While in Cambridge, where she was working at the Metallurgy Department, she wrote her third play, « À contre-voix » (« Counterpoint »), which was translated into English by [[Mary Luckhurst]]. The play was first created in London in 1994 at the « Grace Theatre at the Latchmere Pub », now called Theatre 503.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre503|title=Theater 503}}</ref> It was also performed at the [[Avignon Festival]] that same year, under the direction of Isabelle Andreani. Later, in 2000, « À contre-voix » was brought again to the Avignon Festival, with stage director Serge Dangleterre.

In 1996 she wrote « Musical Box », which was performed in 2001 at the theatre festival of Coye La Forêt <ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.festivaltheatraldecoye.com/HistoriqueProgramme.php|title=Festival Théatral de Coye}}</ref> under the direction of Claude Domenech.

In 2012, she re-wrote a « Tragedy of Medea », entitled « Apatride » (« Stateless ») for herself, a singer and puppets. The play was performed at the Avignon Festival, and then at Ecole Normale Supérieure in 2013, under the direction of Cécile Grandin.

She then wrote ''Puzzle'', a stage adaptation of ''[[Puzzle of a Downfall Child]]'' by [[Jerry Schatzberg]], put on at the Theatre ''La Reine Blanche'' in 2017 under the stage direction of Serge Dangleterre.

She wrote « Le paradoxe des jumeaux » with [[Jean-Louis Bauer]]. It was put on at La Reine Blanche in 2017, for the 150th birthday of Marie Curie. The stage direction was due to Bernadette Le Saché. It was published at L’avant-scène théâtre <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.avantscenetheatre.com/|title=L'Avant-Scène Théâtre}}</ref> together with the translation by Elisabeth Bouchaud of [[Dava Sobel]]’s play « And the Sun stood still ».

In 2021, she created « De la matière dont les rêves sont faits » (« Of such stuff that dreams are made on ») at the Avignon Festival, where she shared the stage direction with actor Grigori Manoukov.

In 2022, she wrote the first episodes of a theatre series ''Les Fabuleuses'' <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/fr/les-fabuleuses-un-documentaire-pour-denoncer-l-effet-matilda-98622/|title=Les Fabuleuses}}</ref> about the life of women scientists that made breakthroughs in physics, but were not remembered through history as male colleagues took the credit and the prizes: ([[Lise Meitner]], [[Jocelyn Bell]], [[Rosalind Franklin]], [[Marthe Gautier]]). 
« Exil intérieur » (« Internal exile ») and « Prix No’Bell » (« No’Bell Prize ») were created at La Reine Blanche in 2022, under the direction of Marie Steen.
« L’affaire Rosalind Franklin » (« The Rosalind Franklin case ») was created in 2024 at La Reine Blanche under the direction of [[:fr:Julie Timmerman]], who will also create « La découvreuse oubliée » about the life and achievements of [[Marthe Gautier]] (« The forgotten discoverer ») in 2026. All the plays are published at « L’avant-scène théâtre ».
